chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Ṭālib ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar and Abā ʿAbd Allah, peace be upon them, about a man who performs the later ʿIshāʾ prayer before the twilight disappears. He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the later night prayer, meaning the ʿIshāʾ prayer
key_terms.زُرَارَةَ: Zurārah, the narrator relating the question and answer
key_terms.سَأَلْتُ: I asked; indicating the transmission of a legal question
key_terms.سُقُوطِ الشَّفَقِ: the disappearance of twilight, a time marker in prayer rulings
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray ʿIshāʾ before the twilight has disappeared?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling regarding the time of the ʿIshāʾ prayer. It reports from Imam al-Bāqir and Imam al-Ṣādiq عليهما السلام that performing the ʿIshāʾ prayer before the disappearance of the twilight is permissible.
